title: GPU scale-harmonizer Terraform module for Private VPC (ASG + Karpenter interoperability)
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a single opinionated Terraform module (gpu-scale-harmonizer) for provisioning GPU node groups inside Private VPC deployments that can operate with both ASG-backed nodegroups and Karpenter-managed node pools. The module must provide safe upgrade paths, automated driver and kernel health checks, and graceful fallback behavior when capacity or driver failures occur. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, CI, and a canary rollout plan for the module.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes a single tf module (gpu_scale_harmonizer) configurable to provision ASG nodegroups or Karpenter node templates via feature flags
Upgrade path documented: blue/green canary flow with node cordon/drain scripts and rollback steps
Automated health checks for GPU driver + kubelet readiness that surface into CloudWatch/Prometheus and the Redwood Console
Terratest suite validating bootstrap (driver install), node readiness, taints/tolerations, and scale-up/down with both ASG and Karpenter in a Private VPC test cluster
CI pipeline runs plan/apply against a disposable terraform workspace and gates with smoke tests and cost-safety timeouts
Module outputs for nodegroup identifiers, instance profile ARNs, and fallback pool identifiers for use by autoscale policies and runtime routing
tasks: Design module interface and variable list (instance types, GPU SKU, driver strategy, kubelet args, taints, labels, min/max/desired)
Define feature flag: use_karpenter = true|false and document expected lifecycle differences
Implement ASG variant with launch template abstraction and secure AMI/driver provisioning via SSM parameter reference
Implement Karpenter variant that renders KarpenterProvisioner CRs and node-template metadata via Terraform provider
Add preflight checks: VPC subnet capacity, IAM role/policies, KMS keys for AMI access, ENI limits per instance family
Implement health-check sidecar script invoked by node bootstrapping to verify NV driver, nvidia-smi, and GPU metrics export
Add graceful upgrade hooks: cordon new nodes, allow KV cache warmup window, drain old nodes with disruptor detection
Write Terratest suites and local emulator tests for both variants
Create CI jobs: tf fmt/validate, plan (drift detection), apply (disposable), smoke e2e, destroy
Author Confluence design doc and run design review with Security and SRE
Create canary rollout playbook and runbook for customer-facing incidents
notes: Design trade-off: keeping single module surface vs separate asg/karpenter modules. We chose single module with a clear feature flag because many customers will migrate between ASG and Karpenter and we want schema-level parity.

Karpenter has no direct API for managing ASG nodegroups—module will avoid trying to reconcile ASG-managed nodes when use_karpenter=true. Instead, it will emit metadata and a helper output to migrate workloads.

Driver installation is brittle across OS/kernel patches. We rely on an AMI baking pipeline for baseline drivers and a small bootstrap that validates & optionally sideloads drivers from a signed S3 artifact for emergency rollbacks.
We will include a 'safe_scale' flag that enforces conservative scale rates and prevents aggressive churn during upgrades to protect KV cache and streaming latency SLOs.
Metrics to monitor: node_ready_fraction, gpu_driver_loaded, nvidia_smi_count, node_boot_time, ASG_health_events, karpenter_provisioner_failures
review_feedback: SRE: add canary percentage and automated rollback if GPU-failure-rate > 2% over 5m
Security: ensure instance profile has least privilege for driver S3 access; prefer KMS envelope encryption for AMI artifacts
Platform: add outputs for node pool tagging convention so Console can correlate costs
PM: include toggle to opt into NVidia MIG partitioning for A100/RTX-class SKUs in future iteration
